The responsibility to set priorities and use criteria implies that whenever the appropriate information is available, the Secretary should specify uniform management policies for lands with similar ecological and physical characteristics, and set priorities so that lands of unique value are protected. The May 5 memorandum fails to do this, in spite of substantial evidence of environmental harm caused by ORVs. The "use criteria" and "operating criteria" set forth by the Secretary merely paraphrase E.O. 11644. They make no progress towards establishing a concrete set of use priorities. The draft statement then undermines the entire effort by implying a set of priorities that provide inadequate protection for environmental values. Hence, neither the memorandum nor the draft statement defines priorities that adequately fulfill Departmental responsibilities.
D. Failure to provide a detailed statement of the impacts of ORV use.
Section 102(2)(c) of NEPA requires that an environmental impact statement contain " ... a detailed statement by the responsible official on --
(i) the environmental impact of the proposed action ..."
